quiz.question: Which data structure maps each keyword to the posts that contain it?
quiz.explanation: An inverted index stores keyword → post IDs, so search is a lookup rather than a scan of every post.

quiz.question: Why is post search a write-heavy problem as well as a read-heavy one?
options: Every new post and every like updates the index
Users search more than they post
quiz.explanation: Posts and likes arrive at huge rates, and each one must be reflected in the index.

quiz.question: How can very frequent like-count updates be made cheaper?
options: Batch them and update the index periodically
Rebuild the whole index per like
quiz.explanation: Approximate, batched like counts are good enough for ranking and cut write load dramatically.

quiz.question: What is a good way to serve repeated popular queries quickly?
options: Cache search results, e.g. at a CDN or cache layer
Add more columns to the posts table
quiz.explanation: Popular queries repeat, so caching their results avoids recomputing them on every request.
